intelligence.enrichment: Lime water turns milky when carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide to form insoluble tiny white particles of calcium carbonate and water. Carbon dioxide in air reacts with calcium hydroxide, producing insoluble calcium carbonate particles, and those particles make the solution look milky. The learner correctly applies this rule: Lime water turns milky when carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide to form insoluble tiny white particles of calcium carbonate and water. Lime water turns milky because air makes clear water dirty.
